title: A restale that hits a RUNNING cell is lost: only reactive-push seeds record it, every other path is overwritten by the result merge
evidence: restale! sets STALE unconditionally, RUNNING included (deps.jl:811-817). The comment on `_DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING` (server.jl:935-948) explains that mark_result! then overwrites that STALE with FRESH. The fix for that was applied at ONE caller: `_reactive_refresh!` notes the dirty bit for its seed cells only (server.jl:798), not for the dependents it restales a few lines later (806). Every other caller restales running cells without the note: update_source!'s dependent cascade (deps.jl:1224), server_src_changed (5541/5547), _restale_side! (2597), the pkg-op wipe (server_history.jl:240) and rerun-all (server_complete.jl:3209). The merges at 4842/5214 only consult the dirty set and src_hash. Commit 967f2ff4 ('Don't lose a reactive push that lands mid-run') shows this was fixed caller-by-caller. Separately, dirty entries are popped only by a successful merge or `_hold_locked!`. The error/blocked exits of `_eval_one_run!` (server.jl:4666, 4726-4727, 4767-4768, 4536) leave them behind, so the cell's NEXT successful run is restaled and re-executed for no reason.
failure_scenario: Serial runner, cell B (reads x) is computing. The user edits upstream cell A (writes x). update_source! restales A and, via dependents_of, B (RUNNING to STALE, no dirty note). B's in-flight result for the OLD x arrives, src_hash is unchanged and B is not in _DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING, so mark_result! makes B FRESH. The runner then runs A. Nothing restales B again because staleness propagates only at edit time. B sits FRESH showing a value computed from the previous A. The same thing happens with a /src hot-reload or a dependent of a reactive seed.
suggested_direction: Put the rule inside restale!: if c.state == RUNNING, set a per-cell `rerun_after::Bool` (or keep RUNNING with a pending-rerun bit) instead of changing state. Have the single merge function honour it and clear it on every exit path, including error and blocked. Delete `_DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING` and the caller-side bookkeeping.
verify_reasoning: Traced. restale! sets STALE unconditionally. Only _reactive_refresh! records seed cells in _DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING, and it does not record the dependents it restales. Here is the failure: update_source! copies RUNNING to B's new Cell, then restales it as a dependent of the edited A. B's in-flight result arrives, the merge (server.jl:4828-4844) finds the same src_hash and no dirty entry, and mark_result! sets B FRESH. Running A afterwards does not restale its dependents. Not verified: the leftover-dirty-entry sub-claim on error exits.

title: STALE-while-executing breaks every consumer that reads RUNNING as 'in flight' (Stop, region-busy, wedge detector)
evidence:
`state` encodes two things: whether the cell needs a run, and whether it is executing. Once restale! (or a direct write) flips an executing cell to STALE:
- cancel_run! (server_complete.jl:117) builds its target list from `_running_kernels`, which keeps only `c.state == RUNNING` (168). If it is empty it returns without cancelling anything (118).
- `_regions_in_use` marks a region busy only for RUNNING cells (3479).
- `_reconcile_stale_runner!` treats 'pending STALE work and nothing RUNNING' as a wedged runner (3127-3130). After _RUNNER_STALE_AFTER (600 s) plus 3 sweeps it deletes `_RUNNERS[nb.id]` and starts a second runner (3147-3154) while the first is still inside `_eval_one!`. The first runner's `finally` (5370-5372) then deletes the second runner's flag.
- `_reconcile_nb_runs!` drops `_RUN_SINCE` and clears the `_REGION_PREPARING` marker for a cell that is still being prepared (3082).
failure_scenario: A dashboard notebook has been draining for more than 10 minutes. A long region cell is running when a `reactive` write restales it (RUNNING to STALE, eval continues on the worker). (a) The user presses Stop: `_running_kernels` finds no RUNNING cell, cancel_run! returns, and the computation keeps going. (b) About 15 s later the wedge detector decides the runner is wedged and starts a second runner. When the first eval finishes, both runners loop over `_next_stale_cell` (serialized only by the eval mutex), and the bookkeeping in `_RUNNERS` is now wrong. (c) The region is no longer counted busy by the RUNNING test while it computes.
suggested_direction: Keep execution as its own fact that only the runner owns, e.g. an `inflight` record set at dispatch and cleared at merge. Make STALE mean only 'needs a run'. Stop, busy, wedge and orphan checks should read the in-flight record, not `state`.
verify_reasoning: Traced. _running_kernels filters on `c.state == RUNNING`, and cancel_run! returns early when that list is empty, so Stop does nothing for an executing cell that was restaled to STALE. _reconcile_stale_runner! counts pending STALE work with no RUNNING cell as a wedge. _RUNNER_STARTED is stamped only when the runner starts, so after a drain longer than 600 s plus three sweeps it clears _RUNNERS and starts a second runner while the first is still inside _eval_one!. _regions_in_use counts only RUNNING cells.

title: _eval_one_run! writes failure transitions to a captured Cell that update_source! may have replaced, which can leave the live cell RUNNING forever
evidence: update_source! builds brand-new Cell objects for EVERY cell on any edit (deps.jl:1175, 1210), copying `state` from the old object (1183). `_eval_one!` receives the Cell captured by the runner (5337-5340) and, after long off-lock phases (region bring-up, about 90 s cold; presync), calls mark_blocked!/mark_errored!/mark_running!/_broadcast_progress on that captured object (4526, 4536, 4726, 4767, 4784). Only the success merge re-resolves the cell by id (4828-4831), and so does `_hold_locked!` (4563). In addition, the `_REGION_PREPARING` marker pushed at 4495 is cleared only at dispatch (4776) or when the cell stops being RUNNING (3082). The failure exits of `_prepare_region_for_cell!` never clear it, and the orphan healer skips any cell with the marker (3100).
failure_scenario: A region cell R is marked RUNNING at 4497 and its region worker starts cold. During the 90 s bring-up the user edits any other cell, so update_source! replaces R with R2, which carries RUNNING. The allocation then disappears, and mark_blocked!(R, WAIT_QUEUED) at 4526 updates the detached R. The browser is sent R's BLOCKED JSON, but the report holds R2 = RUNNING. Nothing re-runs R2: the runner only takes STALE cells, the orphan healer skips it because of the leftover _REGION_PREPARING marker, and the wedge detector sees a RUNNING cell and stands down. `_regions_in_use` also counts the region busy forever, so the node is never released. The next full-state pull flips the page back to a permanent spinner.
suggested_direction: Never hold a Cell across an unlock. Pass the cell id plus the src_hash snapshot, and do every transition through one `with_cell(nb, id, expect_hash) do c ... end` that re-resolves the cell and drops stale transitions. Clear the preparing marker in a `finally` around `_prepare_region_for_cell!`. Better still, make update_source! update cells in place instead of replacing objects.
verify_reasoning: Traced. update_source! replaces every Cell object (report.cells = newr.cells) and copies `state`. _prepare_region_for_cell! pushes the _REGION_PREPARING marker, marks the captured cell RUNNING, and on failure calls mark_blocked!/mark_errored! on that captured object. The marker is cleared only at dispatch (4776) or when _reconcile_nb_runs! sees the cell stop RUNNING (3082). If the replacement is still RUNNING, the orphan healer skips it because of the marker, the runner only takes STALE cells, and the wedge detector stands down while a cell is RUNNING. The worker-could-not-start error path hits this as well as the allocation-gone path.

title: update_source! carries state but drops BLOCKED reason/region, rev, and runtime effect flags on every edit
evidence: The carry-over block copies output, state, deps, binds and interp (deps.jl:1182-1186) and nothing else. The parsed cell starts with blocked="", blocked_region="", blocked_at=0, rev=0 (engine.jl:195), and flags rebuilt from the header, which deliberately omits `_INTERNAL_FLAGS` including `:volatile_declared/:everywhere_declared` (engine.jl:365). The BLOCKED state (commit ab323e83) and the declared effects were added after this carry-over was written and never added to it. `_reestablish_effects!` runs only at load (server.jl:557).
failure_scenario: (1) Cell R is BLOCKED with WAIT_QUEUED on region gpu. The user edits an unrelated cell, and R2 is BLOCKED with blocked="" and blocked_region="". `_reconcile_blocked_regions!` filters on `blocked == WAIT_QUEUED` (3200), so it never resumes asking the scheduler or re-arms R2 when the node is granted. `_regions_in_use` (3484) stops counting the wait, and the header shows a reason-less blocked state. R2 stays BLOCKED until someone presses Run-all. (2) A CODE cell that declared `slate_effect(:everywhere)` (a package op registrar) loses `:everywhere_declared` on any edit, so `_prime_namespace!` stops priming it on a newly started region worker and region cells hit UndefVarError. (3) A cell that called `Sweep.connected(host)` loses `:volatile_declared` and becomes memoizable again, so the next cascade restores the stale sign-in answer, which is the failure remotestore.jl:125-129 says the flag exists to prevent.
suggested_direction: Reconcile cells in place: keep the old Cell object for unchanged src_hash and only replace source-derived fields. If that is not done, move all runtime state into one struct (`CellRuntime`) that update_source! copies as a single unit, so a new field cannot be left out again.
correction: R2 is not stranded on every path. When a node is granted, _restale_region_cells! picks cells by their region tag (_cell_region), not by blocked_region. _region_recoverable accepts any BLOCKED cell whose blocked != WAIT_LOCKED, and that includes blocked="". So if the placement task that was already running completes, R2 is re-armed. What is lost is the supervisor's re-kick of placement, and the cell's contribution to the region-busy count.
verify_reasoning: The carry-over copies state but not blocked, blocked_region, blocked_at, rev or the internal flags. _reconcile_blocked_regions! and _regions_in_use key on blocked == WAIT_QUEUED and on blocked_region, so the supervisor stops re-kicking placement for that cell. Items (2) and (3) duplicate finding 9.

title: Three different implementations of 'the worker's namespace was replaced, invalidate its cells', with conflicting scope and locked-cell policy
evidence: (a) GateKernel.prepare! calls `reset_all!(report)` when a local worker is respawned (gate_kernel.jl:1374). It runs inside every kernel op, OFF nb.lock (eval_capture calls prepare! at 1458). It wipes EVERY cell of the report, region cells included, sets output=nothing, and neither bumps rev nor unblocks. (b) `_restale_side!` (server.jl:2591-2600) touches only `kind == CODE` cells on that side, deliberately bypasses the locked guard ('their frozen result restores into the new process'), keeps outputs and bumps rev. (c) `_reestablish_fresh_namespace!` (5274-5280) restales every auto-running kind (its comment records the bug where a JOB cell left FRESH across a restart broke its card) but goes through restale!, so locked FRESH cells stay FRESH in a blank namespace.
failure_scenario: (a) The local main worker OOMs while a region cell holds a multi-hour result on a healthy region worker. The next main-kernel eval calls prepare!, which calls reset_all!, and the region cell goes STALE with its output erased, triggering a recompute that nothing required. This happens off nb.lock, concurrently with HTTP/state readers and the runner. (b) A region worker is reaped and `_restale_side!` runs. A JOB cell on that region stays FRESH while its channel/bindings are gone, which is the exact bug (c)'s comment says was fixed for the main kernel. (c) After a main-worker swap detected by ns_gen, a locked FRESH cell keeps state FRESH with no binding in the new namespace. `_self_heal_locked!` only targets STALE locked cells (server.jl:997-1000), so readers re-run against an undefined name.
suggested_direction: One function `invalidate_side!(nb, side; reason)` under nb.lock, called from one place (the hub's worker-generation change detection). It should cover all runnable kinds, treat a locked cell as 'restore pending' rather than FRESH, keep outputs for display, and bump rev. Remove reset_all! from GateKernel.prepare!, because the engine layer should not mutate the report's cell state.
correction: Scenario (b) is wrong. _cell_region returns "" for every JOB cell, which pins JOB to the main kernel. No JOB cell can be on a region side, so _restale_side! for a region never involves one. Scenario (c) applies only when ns_gen changes without prepare!'s `replaced` branch, for example a pool adopt or reprovision. A dead-worker respawn already runs reset_all!, which turns locked cells STALE.
verify_reasoning: The three implementations exist and differ as described. GateKernel.prepare! calls reset_all! on a replaced worker, wiping every cell including region cells and clearing their output. _restale_side! covers CODE cells only, bypasses the lock guard and keeps outputs. _reestablish_fresh_namespace! restales every runs_automatically kind through the guarded restale!, so locked FRESH cells stay FRESH. Scenarios (a) and (c) are consistent with the code. Scenario (b) is wrong; see correction.

title: 'Executable cell' is re-tested as kind == CODE in state consumers, so JOB/WEB cells escape Stop, preemption, side invalidation and package-change restale
evidence: engine.jl defines `analyzes_like_code` (CODE, JOB) and `runs_automatically` (not TOOL), and `_batch_cells`/`_reestablish_fresh_namespace!` use them. The state consumers hard-code CODE instead: `_running_kernels` (`c.kind == CODE && c.state == RUNNING`), `_preempt_victims`, `_restale_side!`, `_watchdog_scan!`, the pkg-op restale (server_history.jl:240), and `_cell_effect`, which returns PURE for every non-CODE kind before reading any flag.
failure_scenario: A @sweep JOB cell hangs in submission (`run_there` has a 120 s timeout, and a region bring-up can take longer). The user presses Stop. `_running_kernels` excludes the JOB cell, cancel_run! sees nothing running and returns, and the cell keeps going. After `pkg add`, CODE cells are restaled but a JOB cell that `using`s the package is not.
suggested_direction: Add one predicate, e.g. `executes(c) = c.kind != MARKDOWN` (or a CellKind trait), and use it everywhere a consumer asks 'can this be running/stale in a worker'. Grep for `kind == CODE` next to `state` and replace them.
correction: The pkg-op part is weaker than stated. A JOB cell's `using` upstream is a CODE cell and does get restaled; only the JOB cell itself is skipped. This duplicates finding 38.
verify_reasoning: Traced. `_running_kernels` (server_complete.jl:165-169) keeps only `c.kind == CODE && c.state == RUNNING`, and `cancel_run!` returns at line 118 when that list is empty. `_preempt_victims` (server.jl:5031), `_restale_side!` (server.jl:2595), `_watchdog_scan!` (server.jl:3937) and the pkg-op restale (server_history.jl:240) all hard-code CODE. JOB and WEB cells do reach RUNNING: `_batch_cells` uses `runs_automatically`, and `mark_running!` runs for every dispatched kind. `_cell_effect` returns PURE for any non-CODE cell before it reads a flag (deps.jl:960). If a CODE cell is running on the same kernel, `cancel_eval` interrupts the whole eval and that does cover a JOB cell; a JOB cell running alone is not seen at all.

title: Runtime-declared volatility is only half-wired: downstream memo keys ignore it, and on JOB cells the chip changes nothing
evidence: `_cell_effect` treats `:volatile_declared` like the `volatile` tag (deps.jl:965) and claims to be the single classifier. `_key_poisoned`, which decides whether DOWNSTREAM keys are total, checks only the raw `:volatile` tag (eval.jl:1238). On JOB cells `_cell_effect` returns PURE before it reaches the flag (deps.jl:960), so the declaration from `connected`/`run_there` during a sweep run has no behavioural effect, yet it is rendered as a '⚙ volatile' chip because only `value_identity` is in `_EFFECT_SILENT`.
failure_scenario: Cell V: `ok = Sweep.connected(host)`. Cell D (reads ok, slow enough to be auto-cached) renders a status panel. V is correctly never cached, but D's memo key digests only upstream SOURCES, which have not changed. Next session, after the user has signed out, V re-runs and returns false, while D restores the cached 'connected' panel. The notebook contradicts the padlock, which is the scenario remotestore.jl:125-129 was written to stop. On a @sweep job cell the user sees 'volatile' that affects neither caching nor routing.
suggested_direction: Have `_key_poisoned` call `_cell_effect(c) == VOLATILE` instead of reading flags, so every consumer reads the same classifier. Then either give JOB cells a defined meaning for volatile or stop declaring/rendering it for them (add 'volatile' to the silent list when kind == job).
verify_reasoning: `_key_poisoned` (eval.jl:1234-1241) checks `:nocache`/`:volatile` and never `:volatile_declared`. `_memo_key` digests upstream `src_hash` only, so a reader of a declared-volatile cell gets a stable key and is cached. `_apply_cell_effects!` adds `:volatile_declared` regardless of kind. For JOB cells, `_cell_effect` returns PURE first, `_memoizable` rejects non-CODE, and `_reestablish_effects!` skips non-CODE, so the flag does nothing. view.js `_EFFECT_SILENT` silences only `value_identity`, so the chip still shows 'volatile'. This overlaps findings 29, 41 and 43.

title: State writes bypass the transition helpers: direct `c.state = STALE` and helpers without rev bump or unblock
evidence:
- `set_cell_flag!` restales with `c.state = STALE` (server_agentops.jl:1222). That skips restale!'s locked guard, `_unblock!` and bump_rev!.
- rerun-all (server_complete.jl:3209) and the pkg-op path (server_history.jl:240) write STALE onto RUNNING, BLOCKED and TOOL cells alike.
- The played-cell branch of `_force_cell!` and edit_cell (`c.state = STALE; true`) leaves the blocked fields set.
- `_restale_side!` hand-inlines restale! without the guard.
- `revert_running!` and `reset_all!` neither bump rev nor unblock.
- The page drops `refresh:`/`celldone:` patches whose rev is not newer when the output is unchanged (view.js:1616-1617, 1695). A state-only change without a bump therefore depends on a later full-state pull to become visible.
failure_scenario: Toggling a re-run flag through set_cell_flag! on a locked FRESH cell restales it despite the lock, breaking the 'only its own ▶ restales a locked cell' rule restale! enforces. Rerun-all during a run flips the in-flight cell to STALE, and its result then marks it FRESH: the restale is lost, the same as finding 1. A cell restaled with no rev bump keeps the previous rev, so a later patch for it at the same rev is ignored by the browser until a resync.
suggested_direction: Make `state` writable only through the helpers. Rename the field (e.g. `_state`) and give it a `transition!(c, to; reason)` that applies the guard, the unblock and the rev bump in one place. Express rerun-all and pkg-op as `restale!(c; force=true)`.
correction: `_restale_side!` skipping the locked guard is intentional: its comment says locked cells must go stale too, because the new process does not hold their result. It does call `_unblock!` and `bump_rev!`, so it does not belong on this list.
verify_reasoning: The direct writes exist as cited, with no unblock and no rev bump: `set_cell_flag!` (server_agentops.jl:1222), rerun-all (server_complete.jl:3209), the pkg-op restale (server_history.jl:240), and the played-cell branch `c.state = STALE; true` in `_force_cell!`/`edit_cell!`. `revert_running!` and `reset_all!` neither bump rev nor unblock. `revIsNew` (view.js:1613-1617) drops a payload at an equal rev when the output is unchanged, so a state-only change with no bump can be invisible until a full pull. The lost-restale outcome during rerun-all depends on runner timing I did not trace.

title: Stop does not stop a serial run: the runner keeps draining, and downstream of the stopped cell runs against its previous values
evidence: cancel_run! sets only `_PARALLEL_CANCEL[nb.id] = true` and messages the workers. `_PARALLEL_CANCEL` is read only inside `_run_code_batch!` (server.jl:5118), which returns false whenever `_region_active(nb)` (5101) and for 0/1-cell batches. The serial loop (5320-5342) never consults any stop state: after the interrupted cell merges as ERRORED it calls `_next_stale_cell` again and runs the next STALE cell. Two further holes: `_run_code_batch!` resets `_PARALLEL_CANCEL[nb.id] = false` at batch start (5109), erasing a Stop issued between batches or during bring-up; and `cancel_run!` returns immediately when no cell is RUNNING (line 118), for example while the runner is in `_reestablish_fresh_namespace!`/`resolve_usings!` spawning a remote worker. Nothing skips cells downstream of an ERRORED one: `_eval_one_run!` only checks for BLOCKED upstreams (4676-4701).
failure_scenario: A notebook with a region (always serial). Run-all, then press Stop (runstatus.js:257 labels it 'Stop the run') while cell 3 of 20 runs on the cluster. Cell 3 errors with InterruptException, and the runner immediately starts cell 4, then 5, and so on to the end. A cell downstream of cell 3 runs against the namespace's previous value of cell 3's outputs (the graceful stop preserved it) and goes FRESH, showing results inconsistent with its ERRORED upstream. The user must press Stop once per remaining cell.
suggested_direction: Make a stop a hub-side state that the runner consults: a per-notebook 'stop requested at generation G' that `_run_loop!` checks before every step and that `_run_code_batch!` does not reset. Mark not-yet-run cells (at least the transitive dependents of stopped cells) as held/stopped rather than leaving them STALE for the next pass.
correction: In parallel mode with no region, Stop does work for cells the batch has not started: run_scheduled marks them ERRORED (5118-5126). The defect is specific to the serial path, which every region notebook uses.
verify_reasoning: Traced. cancel_run! (server_complete.jl:115-136) sets only _PARALLEL_CANCEL[nb.id]=true, then asks the running kernels to stop. _PARALLEL_CANCEL is read at exactly one place, server.jl:5118, inside _run_code_batch!. That function returns false when _region_active(nb) (5101) or when fewer than 2 cells are runnable (5098), so it never reaches that read in those cases. The serial loop in _run_loop! (server.jl:5323-5342) checks only _RUNNER_CANCEL, which is set only on notebook close (server_complete.jl:4396). It then picks _next_stale_cell again and runs it. _eval_one_run! (4676-4701) holds a cell back only for a BLOCKED upstream, never an ERRORED one, and the worker's graceful stop keeps the namespace (worker.jl:1090-1093), so downstream cells read the old values. The two further holes also hold. _run_code_batch! resets the flag to false at 5109, after prepare! (5103), so a Stop pressed during bring-up is erased. cancel_run! returns at line 118 when no cell is RUNNING, and it does nothing else that the serial path reads. PARALLEL_DEFAULT is true (server.jl:4932), so the serial path is the one that matters for region notebooks, for notebooks with parallel turned off, and for single stale cells.

title: Cell.state does double duty: restale overwrites RUNNING, so Stop and preemption cannot see in-flight cells
evidence: `restale!` sets `c.state = STALE` unconditionally (deps.jl:814). `_reactive_refresh!` records the overwrite in a side set (`_DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING`, server.jl:798) but leaves the cell STALE while its worker eval is still in flight. No separate in-flight record exists on the hub; the worker has one (`_RUNNING_TASKS`) that the hub never asks for.
failure_scenario: A dashboard: a long cell reads a reactive that an @onclick handler writes in a loop. Each write restales the running cell to STALE. The user presses Stop: `_running_kernels` returns empty, so `cancel_run!` returns at line 118 and nothing is sent to the worker. The cell keeps computing, then re-runs because it is dirty. The same cell edited after a restale is not preempted, because `_preempt_victims` skips non-RUNNING cells.

(server.jl:796-799) notes the RUNNING cell in _DIRTY_WHILE_RUNNING and then restales it, while its worker eval is still in flight. title: Region namespace loss is handled per event site, not by generation; an in-place worker swap leaves region cells FRESH with their values gone
evidence: The main kernel detects a fresh namespace generically: `_MAIN_GEN` is compared with `_worker_key` at the top of each drain and restales everything. Regions instead call `_restale_side!` at five specific event sites (placement granted, reap, explicit reap, prepare-replace, restart_region!). `prepare!` can bump `ns_gen` in place on a region kernel through a cold spawn or adopt (remote.jl:3213, 3368; for example payload drift in `_worker_current`, or a dead worker). `_prepare_region_for_cell!` then only primes and calls `_rearm_locked!`, which re-arms locked cells only. ns_gen-keyed dedups re-ship values INTO the region, but values computed ON the region are not restaled.
failure_scenario: A region worker is OOM-killed between runs. The next region cell's `prepare!` cold-spawns a replacement (ns_gen+1). Upstream region cell `model = train(...)` is still FRESH on the host, so it does not re-run, and the downstream same-side cell fails with UndefVarError(:model). The cross-side `cellkey` memo-restore patch in transfer_binding! (server.jl:4378) only covers readers on OTHER sides, and only if the writer was memoized.

Removing the `volatile_declared` chip from a CODE cell in the tag editor (`set_cell_tags!` keeps only :opaque) silently makes that cell cacheable again.

title: Reattach reaps a worker that is busy computing: every attach-ladder liveness test assumes the gate answers on an interactive thread, but KaimonGate serves requests on the default pool
evidence: Commit 6691037a6 (2026-10-09) changed a failed __slate_env_info from 'keep' to 'replace'. Its stated premise is 'The gate answers on the worker's interactive thread, so a worker busy with a cell still answers' (remote.jl:2929). KaimonGate's message_loop hands every request to `Threads.@spawn _serve_request(...)`, which runs on the default pool (gate_protocol.jl:767). server.jl:2696 (commit 076ab98f1) states the correct behaviour: 'the gate answers each request on a default-pool thread, which cells can keep busy', and that is why the liveness sweep falls back to `_telemetry_fresh`. The attach ladder has no such fallback. The park check (env_info, 5s), the record dial (connect_tcp! pings, 5s), the probe dial (15s, then `reap_remote_worker`) and `_worker_current` (6s + 20s, then reap) all read silence as 'wedged'. In the stale-payload branch, a __slate_running timeout is swallowed as 'not busy' (remote.jl:2957-2963), so a busy stale worker is reaped as well. The function header (2909-2910) still says 'A failed env_info call counts as yes', which contradicts the code.
failure_scenario:
1. A `:tunnel` region worker runs a CPU-bound cell (Threads.@threads or BLAS) that occupies every default thread.
2. The ssh session drops. `_drop_signed_out_wire!` drops the wire with hold=false.
3. A key sign-in succeeds, ERRORED region cells are restaled and the runner calls prepare!.
4. The record dial's ping cannot be scheduled within 5s, so the record is cleared.
5. The roster probe finds the worker alive (pgrep / fresh stats) and dials for 15s. The ping again cannot be served, so the hub logs 'wedged/half-dead' and calls `reap_remote_worker`, which sends SIGKILL to the worker mid-computation.
If the dial does get through, `_worker_current` waits 26s for env_info and reaps on the same reasoning. Telemetry, which comes from an interactive thread, shows the worker at 100% CPU the whole time, and the post-attach sweep would have called it 'busy, not gone'.
suggested_direction: Make one liveness oracle used by both the sweep and the attach ladder: telemetry/stats freshness plus process presence decides alive vs dead, and gate silence alone only ever means 'busy'. Never reap on silence while telemetry or stats are fresh. Better still, have KaimonGate serve a small set of liveness/introspection tools (ping, __slate_running, __slate_env_info) on the interactive thread, so the stated premise becomes true.
correction: BLAS does not occupy Julia scheduler threads beyond the one that calls it, so the BLAS example is weak. The trigger is a cell that saturates every default-pool thread: `Threads.@threads`, or many spawned tasks that never yield. A long stop-the-world GC also qualifies. Workers launch with `--threads=N,1` or `N,2`, so the cell's own eval task occupies one of the N.
verify_reasoning: gate_protocol.jl:764-767 hands every request, pings included, to `Threads.@spawn _serve_request(...)` with no threadpool argument, so it runs on the default pool. Nothing is fast-pathed between deserialize (755) and the spawn. Commit 6691037a6 rests on the opposite premise. It replaced `catch; return true` with two env_info tries (6s, then 20s), and on failure `attached!` (remote.jl:3226-3235) runs `reap_remote_worker`, which sends TERM and then KILL. The probe branch (3329-3343) reaps after a failed 15s dial for the same reason ('a merely-busy worker answers on its interactive thread'). title: A dropped wire abandons the in-flight eval only on the hub side; reattach re-dispatches the same cell id concurrently and the worker's cid-keyed run set corrupts
evidence: `_drop_kernel_conn!` disconnects the DEALER so the blocked eval_capture errors and the cell becomes ERRORED. Nothing tells the worker, which keeps evaluating. `attached!` (remote.jl:3223) never asks the reattached worker what it is still running and never cancels it. On the worker, `__slate_eval` registers `_RUNNING_TASKS[cid] = current_task()` and its `finally` does `delete!(_RUNNING_TASKS, cid)` (worker.jl:1043,1052), so the entry is keyed by cell id with no run token. A second eval of the same cid overwrites the first's entry, and whichever finishes first deletes the other's. The orphan reconciler (server.jl:3074) then sees a RUNNING cell that is absent from __slate_running on two sweeps and reverts it to STALE while its eval is still in flight.
failure_scenario:
1. A long region cell C runs on a :direct worker.
2. A network partition lasts longer than the grace period (45s). Telemetry rides the same lost link, so it is stale and the sweep drops the wire. C shows ERRORED, but the worker is still computing it.
3. The partition heals and the user re-runs C. prepare! reattaches to the same worker by record (namespace and payload are current), and C is dispatched again. Two evaluations of C now mutate the same globals concurrently.
4. The first finishes and deletes `_RUNNING_TASKS["C"]`. Two sweeps later the reconciler resets the second run to STALE and the runner starts a third.
Cancel can now interrupt only the task that currently owns the key.
suggested_direction: Treat 'worker still running cells' as state to reconcile on every attach. After any (re)attach, call __slate_running and, for each cell the hub does not consider in flight, either cancel it or adopt it (wait for its result instead of re-dispatching). Key worker run registrations by a hub-issued run id, not the cell id.
verify_reasoning: `_drop_kernel_conn!` (gate_kernel.jl:1306-1319) only disconnects locally and sends nothing to the worker. `attached!` (remote.jl:3223-3251) checks env_info, and checks `__slate_running` only on the stale-payload path. It never reconciles or cancels evals still in flight from the old wire. `__slate_eval` (worker.jl:1042-1052) does `_RUNNING_TASKS[cid] = current_task()` and `delete!(_RUNNING_TASKS, cid)` in its `finally`. The key has no run token and nothing serialises evals of the same cid: `_eval_one` takes no namespace-wide lock. A second dispatch therefore overwrites the entry, and the first run's `finally` removes the second's. `_reconcile_nb_runs!` (server.jl:3074-3112) then sees the RUNNING cell absent from `actual.ids` on two sweeps and calls `revert_running!`, so the runner dispatches it again. I traced every step. The precondition is a partition longer than the grace while a region cell runs, followed by a re-run.

title: Two remote kill implementations: restart uses SIGTERM-only teardown that deletes the manifest, roster reap uses TERM→KILL with full cache eviction
evidence: `teardown_remote!(kill=true)` runs `pkill -u $USER -f [w]orker-PORT.jl` with the default SIGTERM, does not kill the worker's children, does not `_mark_reaped!`, `_evict_worker_conn!`, `_release_region_claim!` or `_peer_route_forget!`, and then deletes .jl/.json/.state/.stats. `reap_remote_worker` exists precisely because 'a FROZEN or wedged worker ... never processes SIGTERM ... so the SIGKILL is what actually frees its LISTEN port and RAM' (remote.jl:6516-6518). The notebook Restart button (restart_kernel! → shutdown!(kill_remote=true) plus _teardown_region!(kill=true)) and restart_region! take the weak path. The roster's per-worker restart (restart_worker!) takes the strong one. Its docstring says 'Manual only — Slate never auto-reaps', but `attached!`, the probe path, region reconcile and region release call it automatically.
failure_scenario:
1. A region worker deadlocks (the GC-callback class of hang).
2. The user presses Restart. teardown sends SIGTERM. Julia's jl_exit runs atexit hooks (KaimonGate stop, _ssh_fwd_killall!), which hang in the deadlocked process, so the process survives.
3. The manifest is already deleted, so the roster never lists it again and no later reap can find it. The spin-guard does not fire because evals > 0.
4. A fresh worker is spawned beside it on the same node. The survivor keeps its RAM/GPU and ports until the allocation ends, or indefinitely on a non-scheduler host.
suggested_direction: Use one `kill_worker!(host, port; label)` for every remote kill: TERM, bounded wait, KILL including children, mark reaped, evict every cache, and delete the manifest only after the process is confirmed gone. `teardown_remote!(kill=true)` should call it. Fix the 'manual only' docstring.
correction: teardown_remote!(kill=true) does evict the parked wire, the attach record and the data tunnels (`_evict_parked!`, `_attach_clear!`, `_evict_data_tunnels!`, `_blob_dport_forget!`). The gap is narrower than 'evicts nothing', but it is real: no SIGKILL, no reap mark, no conn/claim/peer-route eviction, and the manifest is deleted before the process is confirmed gone.
verify_reasoning: `teardown_remote!(kill=true)` (remote.jl:3484-3493) runs `pkill -u $USER -f [w]orker-PORT.jl` (TERM only) and immediately runs `rm -f` on .jl/.json/.state/.stats. Restart (`restart_kernel!` → `shutdown!(kill_remote=true)` + `_teardown_region!(kill=true)`) and `restart_region!` take the weak path. The 'Manual only, never auto-reaps' docstring (6452-6453) and the '/api/reap-worker … Never automatic' comment are contradicted by automatic calls in `attached!` and the probe branch. The failure scenario (SIGTERM not ending a deadlocked Julia process) is plausible rather than demonstrated: Julia turns SIGTERM into an exit on thread 0 that runs atexit hooks, which can hang in a deadlocked process. The duplication and its drift are confirmed.

evidence: `_supervise_runs!` iterates every notebook and every kernel in one task. `_liveness_sweep!` makes a blocking `_tool(__slate_running; timeout=8)` per kernel. For the reason in finding 1, any busy worker costs the full 8s each sweep before the telemetry fallback applies. `_heal_dead_wire!` → `_drop_kernel_conn!` does `lock(k.lock)`. Kernels hold that lock across long operations: a cold spawn (minutes), and `shutdown!(wait=true)` → `teardown_remote!`'s ssh pkill/rm, with k.conn still set. `_region_kernel!` already knows this hazard and spawns the drop on its own task (server.jl:2342-2346); the supervisor calls it inline.

evidence: _region_has_live_workers uses list_remote_workers(h) = last(_list_remote_workers(h)), which returns Any[] when the host could not be asked (remote.jl:6246). failure_scenario: A notebook holds a node for 20 min. Its cells are FRESH and the user is reading output. The laptop sleeps or the VPN drops, so the login-node session is lost and the region kernel's conn goes to nothing. On the next 60 s sweep, _region_serves_kernel is false, no cell is RUNNING or BLOCKED, and the grant is older than 300 s, so reconcile runs. Listing workers fails (offline), the region reads as 'no live workers', and region_release! runs. Its reap also fails ('releasing without reaping'), region_forget_placement! drops the hub's belief, and scancel either fails (session down) or succeeds once the session flaps back. Either the node is released under the user, or the hub forgets a job that still holds a live worker with all the session's state, and the next cell starts a second worker on it after the 120 s _GAVE_UP window.

correction: Part of the claimed downstream effect is speculative. After _GAVE_UP expires, the next cell run re-finds the job by name. The core defect stands as stated: an unreachable host is read as an empty node, and that triggers a release.

An empty roster makes `any(...)` false, so _region_reconcile_impl! (remote.jl:5944) calls region_release!(r). For a scheduler region r.warm is always 0 (_warm_for, remote.jl:5077), so that guard never blocks. _sweep_dead_regions! (server.jl:3697) reaches reconcile when the region is not in `busy` and _region_serves_kernel is false. title: SLURM name lookup is not scoped to the user; PBS's is (another user's 'slate-<region>' job is adopted)
evidence: _slurm_find_script is `squeue -h -n <name> -o ...` with no `-u $USER`. squeue lists every user's jobs by default. The PBS find (`qselect -u "$USER"`), the PBS release (`qselect -N ... -u "$USER"`) and even the SLURM ETA probe in scheduler.jl:186 (`-u "$USER"`) are all user-scoped. The default job name is 'slate-' * r.name (remote.jl:5483), and generic region names such as gpu or cpu collide across users on a shared cluster. The name→job resolution is written about four times per scheduler (find, release, ETA/load, extend), and they have drifted.
failure_scenario: Two Slate users on a SLURM cluster such as Perlmutter both define a region 'gpu'. User B holds 'slate-gpu'. User A's request_allocation! finds B's RUNNING job, so `cur.state !== :none` and A never submits. region_place! routes A to B's node with B's job id, and _await_node_ready! spends 120 s on `srun --jobid=<B's job>` steps, which fail with permission denied. A's cells never get a node while B's job lives, and A's idle or explicit release tries `scancel -n slate-gpu`.
suggested_direction: Add `-u "$USER"` (or `--me`) to the SLURM find. Better still, write the name→job resolution once per scheduler (one `resolve_jobs(kind, host, name)` used by find, release, extend and load), and cancel the specific job ids rather than every job with the name.
correction: `scancel -n slate-gpu` run by A only cancels A's own jobs, because SLURM denies cancelling another user's job. So the release step is a failed command, not damage to B. A is still blocked from ever getting a node.
verify_reasoning: _slurm_find_script (allocation.jl:169-170) is `squeue -h -n <name> -o ...` with no -u/--me. The next minute finds no live workers and releases.
